newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ MCI index again falls through -1.0 on soft TWI.
newsitem.headline: NZ MCI index again falls through -1.0 on soft TWI.

text.p: New Zealand's Monetary Conditions Index (MCI) fell to 101 basis points equivalent in interest rate terms below the Reserve Bank's March assumptions at 2.55 p.m. for the second time on Tuesday.
The MCI measures the degree of variance in money and foreign exchange market conditions from the RBNZ's preferred mix of 90-day rates at 7.5 percent and the Trade-Weighted Index at 68.0.
The 90-day rate was at 7.10 percent and the TWI at 67.19 at about 3.00 p.m. but slipped further to a day's trading low of 67.13 by 3.04 p.m. (0304 GMT) taking the MCI index to -1.03.
Financial markets are wary of a Reserve Bank comment on the loose monetary conditions, even though the bank is expected to sanction an easing in its June 27 Monetary Policy Statement.
Forex dealers said some in the market believed the bank would comment if the MCI remained at more than 100 basis points below the bank's preferred line for a sustained period of time.
